title: The 13 vowels

video.title: Master the Sanskrit sounds (Varnamala series, episode 1)
video.focus: How each vowel is made in the mouth, and the difference between the short and long pairs (इ/ई, उ/ऊ). Notice that the teacher says the final अ in every word.

altVideo.title: संस्कृत वर्णमाला के सभी वर्णों का ज्ञान

idea: A **vowel** (स्वर, svara) is a sound you can sing on its own, with nothing blocking the air. Sanskrit has thirteen: अ आ इ ई उ ऊ ऋ ॠ ऌ ए ऐ ओ औ.

Hindi charts usually show अं and अः in the vowel row. In Sanskrit those two are not vowels: the dot (anusvāra) and the two dots (visarga) are extra sounds that come after a vowel. Tomorrow's lesson is about them.
- Short, one beat (मात्रा, mātrā = a beat of time): अ इ उ ऋ ऌ
- Long, two beats: आ ई ऊ ॠ
- Always long: ए ऐ ओ औ
Length changes meaning. दिन (dina) is a day; दीन (dīna) is poor. Hold the long ones for a full two beats, longer than you would in Hindi.

In Hindi you say राम as "Rām" and drop the last vowel. Sanskrit never drops it: राम is rāma, देव is deva, धर्म is dharma. Every consonant without a mark carries a spoken अ. This is the biggest habit to change, so check it in every word you read this week.
- ऋ is a vowel, not र + इ. Say a short, crisp "ri" with the tongue curled back: ऋषि (ṛṣi), कृपा (kṛpā). South Indian speakers say "ru"; both are heard today.
- ऐ is two sounds in one, a + i, like "ai" in aisle: ऐक्य (aikya). Not the flat "ae" of Hindi है.
- औ is a + u, like "ou" in loud: औषध (auṣadha). Not the "aw" of Hindi और.
ॠ and ऌ are rare. Learn to recognise them (पितॄन् pitṝn, कॢप्त kḷpta) and move on.

examples.meaning: day / poor: short vs long इ
family / river bank: short vs long उ

quiz.q: How many vowels does Sanskrit have?
quiz.why: अ आ इ ई उ ऊ ऋ ॠ ऌ ए ऐ ओ औ. The dot (ं) and two dots (ः) are not vowels.

quiz.q: Which word has a long vowel in its first syllable?
quiz.why: दीन is dīna, with long ī: two beats. दिन and कुल have short vowels.

quiz.q: In Sanskrit, how do you say राम?
quiz.why: Every written अ is spoken. Dropping the final a is a Hindi habit.
ऐ is a two-part vowel, a followed by i. ऐक्य is aikya.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a vowel in Sanskrit?
quiz.why: अं is the vowel अ plus the anusvāra dot. ऋ and ऌ are real vowels, even though ऌ is rare.

extra: Read the vowel row aloud twice, once short-long in pairs (अ आ, इ ई, उ ऊ, ऋ ॠ) and once straight through.
